criteria.title: Nvidia crashes
criteria.rule: NVDA trades at least 50% below its all-time high.
criteria.why: Nvidia is the purest public bet on AI. Every past tech bubble ended with its leader losing more than half its value (Cisco fell ~80% after 2000).
criteria.detail: NVDA at $242.32 vs. all-time high of $242.32 (2026-10-06).

criteria.title: Tech enters a deep bear market
criteria.rule: The Nasdaq-100 is at least 30% below its all-time high.
criteria.why: A bubble bursting drags the whole sector, not just one stock. The Nasdaq-100 fell 33% in 2022 and 83% after the dot-com peak.
criteria.detail: Nasdaq-100 at 31,309 vs. all-time high of 31,309 (2026-10-06).

criteria.title: Big Tech cuts AI spending
criteria.rule: Combined quarterly capex of Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta falls year-over-year.
criteria.why: Hyperscaler data-center spending is the money that funds the whole AI supply chain. When it shrinks, the boom has stopped.
criteria.detail: 2026 Q2: $165.1B combined vs. $88.2B a year earlier.

criteria.title: Compute glut
criteria.rule: Median on-demand H100 rental price falls below $1.00 per GPU-hour.
criteria.why: If GPUs become nearly free to rent, the world built more AI capacity than anyone is willing to pay for — the classic overbuild of a bubble.
